rows.question: does the evidence model distinguish a vendor claim from a bank fact?

probes.observed: the vocabulary is closed and ordered: UNKNOWN < INFERRED < DECLARED < IMPORTED < CONFIGURED < OBSERVED < NETWORK_OBSERVED < RUNTIME_OBSERVED — a vendor claim never outranks the bank's own observation
a vendor document alone yields DECLARED_ONLY with confidence LOW — it cannot reach CONFIRMED because nothing in the bank's estate was read
CAPABILITY_DECLARED, CAPABILITY_OBSERVED and USAGE_OBSERVED are three events with three definitions, so a dashboard cannot collapse them into one green tick
a claim with no citation is refused at construction: evidence must name the record it came from, and the row carries a stable VE- identifier

rows.question: does a vendor document for one product version stay attached to that version?

probes.observed: 8.2.1 versus 8.4.0 -> VERSION_MISMATCH: declared 8.2.1, deployed 8.4.0: a different generation, so the declared crypto inventory does not travel
4 declared capabilities are carried with the verdict and none of them is counted as a vendor capability of this appliance
exact=8.2.1->MATCHED, patch 8.2.1->8.2.2 PARTIAL_MATCH, minor 8.3.0->8.4.0 VERSION_MISMATCH, and 8.10 > 8.9 because versions compare as numbers rather than strings
four different refusals for four different reasons: wrong product, wrong vendor, unversioned deployment and unversioned document — none of them silently MATCHED
a document replaced by a newer one is SUPERSEDED and an old one is EXPIRED, both before any capability is quoted — the version matches and the claim is still refused

with the applicability gate replaced by a constant MATCHED the same 8.2.1 document lights every capability on the 8.4.0 appliance — so the refusal above is the gate doing the work, not a phrase in this paragraph

rows.question: is vendor due diligence a structured record or a status field?

probes.observed: 22 sections are listed; a section that is missing is named rather than scored as zero: vendor_identity, product, product_version, contract, support_lifecycle, end_of_life, …
an empty record scores 0.0% and blocks approval for 6 stated reasons, e.g. the last review is unknown: no verification date, so the age of this evidence is unknown
all 22 sections present, review 365 days old -> COMPLETE, 0 blocker(s)
every section is still on file, and the record is 813 days old, so approval is blocked and the age is stated
a review status outside the five the model accepts raises rather than being stored

rows.question: does the product lifecycle drive the crypto migration answer?

probes.observed: the ladder runs CURRENT -> SUPPORTED -> MAINTENANCE -> END_OF_SUPPORT -> END_OF_LIFE -> RETIRED
the record still says SUPPORTED while support ended on 2025-06-30: the effective state is END_OF_SUPPORT and the drift is reported
past both dates the product is END_OF_LIFE, not merely END_OF_SUPPORT, and the record is flagged unsupported
the same product state appears as its own risk factor with 25 points, so an EOL appliance raises the vendor score instead of sitting beside it as decoration

rows.question: can the estate answer 'which bank systems depend on this vendor product?' — for hardware and for software?

probes.observed: Vendor-X HSM-X500 -> 3 appliance(s) -> 4 application(s) -> 3 service(s) -> ['Card Authorization']; the other vendor's appliance is not counted
three appliances and four applications is not seven of anything — each level is counted on its own, which is the number a risk committee can act on
a vendor with no recorded appliance says so explicitly, so an empty result cannot be read as an all-clear
SDK 4.2 -> 3 applications, 7 containers, 2 systems and 1 critical service — the version filter excludes the 4.1 deployment, which is a different exposure

rows.question: does one capability row show what is declared, what is observed and what is used?

probes.observed: AES-256 shows vendor_declared, bank_observed, production_usage, version_matched and evidence_fresh separately; the single status is CONFIRMED, and a UI does not have to infer it
a capability the vendor declared and a running session exercised is CORROBORATED at HIGH confidence — the one combination that justifies the word verified
every field the review listed is present, including the applicability verdict and the evidence list, and the record holds no key material of any kind
AES-128 observed on the appliance and never declared is recorded at MEDIUM as BANK_OBSERVED_ONLY — it is a finding about the estate, not a gap in the VBOM

the existing `VbomGenerator` row shape gains the evidence type, the applicability verdict, the verification status and both evidence ids — so a VBOM row can be defended one at a time (ML-DSA-65: ML-DSA is a post-quantum construction)

rows.question: does old vendor evidence still look current on the dashboard?

probes.observed: last verified 2024-08-11, 813 days ago -> EXPIRED: last verified 2024-08-11, 813 days ago — more than twice the review window, so it cannot support a current claim
FRESH inside one review window, STALE inside two, EXPIRED beyond that, and UNKNOWN when there is no date at all — a missing date is not treated as fresh
an old document produces VENDOR_EVIDENCE_STALE beside the claim rather than quietly supporting a current answer: VENDOR_DOCUMENT_EXPIRED, VENDOR_EVIDENCE_STALE
an out-of-date document raises VENDOR_DOCUMENT_EXPIRED, not a version mismatch: the event names the reason, so the reviewer is not sent to compare versions that already agree
a claim with no observation date reports UNKNOWN freshness, so 'PQC ready' can never rest on a row nobody can date

rows.question: when the vendor, the SBOM, the CBOM and the runtime disagree, does the VBOM pick a winner?

probes.observed: OpenSSL: vendor 3.0.13, SBOM 3.0.11, runtime 3.0.11 -> CONFLICT; every row is kept and the conflict is the finding
CBOM says AES-256 is supported while the runtime exercised AES-128-GCM: both rows survive, the stronger source is named for triage, and neither overwrites the other
AGREE (two sources, same value), SINGLE_SOURCE (one source, not corroboration) and UNKNOWN (nobody stated it) are distinguished, because a single source is not corroboration
vendor '3.0' against SBOM '3.0.11' is one source saying less, not two sources disagreeing — the difference between PARTIAL and CONFLICT is precision
the vendor row and the observation row group into one CONFIRMED capability with both evidence ids attached, instead of two rows a reader has to reconcile by hand

rows.question: is a vendor risk rating explainable, or a colour somebody typed?

probes.observed: CRITICAL (100/100) from 11 named factors, each with points and a reason: product_lifecycle +25, pqc_capability +20, critical_systems_affected +15, crypto_dependency +15, …
a current product with PQC, a verified deployment, an SBOM and supply-chain evidence scores LOW because no factor applies — the score is computed, not typed
a vendor that states no PQC position scores 20 with the factor marked UNKNOWN; one that declares none scores 30
the score is a pure function of its factors: two runs with the same inputs are identical, so a rating can be reproduced in front of a regulator

limits: no vendor was contacted and no vendor document was parsed from PDF: the declarations here are fixtures shaped like the fields the review named, so the module is graded, not a vendor's paperwork

applicability is computed from vendor, product, version and revision. A vendor that versions its crypto profile separately from its firmware version would need a second identity axis this model does not have
a PATCH-level difference is PARTIAL_MATCH by design; whether the vendor's advisory says the crypto inventory changed inside a patch is a judgement this module hands to a reviewer rather than guessing
freshness needs a date on the evidence. A questionnaire that arrives undated is UNKNOWN, which blocks a claim rather than ageing gracefully into a false green
reconciliation compares string forms of a value. Two sources that name the same thing differently ('AES-256' and 'AES256') will conflict until a normaliser sits in front of it

the dependency chains are assembled from records the bank supplies: appliance to application comes from configuration evidence, application to service from the service register, and neither is discovered by this module
container counts come from the SBOM import, so a container that ships the component without naming it would be missed
risk weights are this artifact's stated weights, visible in the module; a bank with its own risk framework can read the factors and reweight them without changing the evidence
